subject: Capacity booking ladder & GPU cushion options for Sable AI — proposal
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@sable.ai>, Priya Menon <priya.m@sable.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity booking ladder & GPU cushion options for Sable AI — proposal

Jordan / Priya — thanks again for the time today. As promised, attached are three structured options for Dedicated capacity tied to your 1Q product launch. I tried to balance spend predictability with fast activation and a small operational cushion so your latency SLOs are preserved during spikes. Highlights up front:

- Quick summary (see attached worksheet for line-by-line pricing):
  1) Booking Ladder (recommended for forecasted growth) — baseline reserved GPUs + scheduled step-ups. Predictable monthly invoices; lower unit price as you scale. Baseline: 40 GPUs, Step 1 (wk6) +20, Step 2 (mo3) +40 -> 100 total. One month pre-warm credit included.
  2) Slot Priority (dedicated lanes) — smaller baseline (20 GPUs) but dedicated GPU lanes with guaranteed warm KV cache and priority routing. Best for latency-critical endpoints; higher unit cost.
  3) Flex-Reserve (buffered burst + pay-for-use) — minimal committed baseline (10 GPUs) + pooled burst credits. Low upfront, higher variable spend; good if demand is unpredictable.

- Key operational guards we recommend: 10% GPU cushion (to reduce throttling during traffic bursts), step-up windows of 4–8 weeks, and a one-time onboarding credit to offset warm-up usage.

Attached: capacity-options-worksheet.xlsx (breakdown by GPU-hour, monthly invoicing scenarios), Sable-deal-MAP-v2.pdf (mutual action plan).

Questions we still need from your side to firm pricing: preferred activation date (target default: 2027-01-15), procurement cadence (monthly invoicing vs single PO + amortization), and whether you want a private deployment path on our roadmap (adds KMS/air-gapped options and modifies lead time).

Next steps: if you can indicate a preferred option and procurement preference by end of next week we’ll prepare a narrow DocuSign-ready commitment and a transition runbook for your infra team.

Cheers,
Ethan Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Capacity booking ladder & GPU cushion options for Sable AI — proposal

Ethan — thanks for the detailed options, very helpful. A few constraints from our side that will determine which path we can take:

- Procurement: our finance team prefers predictable monthly spend tied to a single PO and prefers not to do variable invoices where possible.
- Security: we are committing to a private deployment in H2; can you show how that affects lead time / ramp?
- Sizing constraint: we need the initial committed baseline to be <= 50 GPUs from a budget perspective.
- Ramp preference: we’d like to limit changes to the first 3 months (ideally a 3-month ramp schedule).

Also, can you include a worst-case latency write-up and a fallback plan (if a burst exceeds reserved capacity, how does graceful degradation work and what are the failover model options)? If possible, please show an example monthly invoice for each option vs forecasted traffic (low/expected/high).

Happy to discuss with Priya and the procurement lead on a short call — are you available Friday afternoon?

Best,
Jordan
Director of Platform, Sable AI
[j.ellis@sable.ai]

Subject: Fwd: Capacity booking ladder — Sable constraints & ask (internal)

Team — forwarding Sable’s constraints (see below). High-level thoughts before I jump on a call with Jordan Friday:

- Procurement wants single-PO predictable monthly spend; that nudges us toward the Booking Ladder with fixed monthly billing (amortize any onboarding credit across first 3 months).
- Budget cap <= 50 GPUs baseline: propose we offer a scaled Booking Ladder that starts at 40 GPUs baseline (fits Sable ask) and provides two scheduled step-ups: +20 at week 6 and +40 by month 3 if traffic materializes. This becomes a 40 -> 60 -> 100 path but initial committed baseline is 40, which aligns with their <=50 constraint.
- Latency / fallback: recommend we include a documented fallback that routes non-critical batch workloads to Spot-backed lanes and configures priority lanes for inference endpoints. Offer 1 month of pre-warm credits and a 10% onboarding credit applied to the first invoice.
- Commercial ask: to preserve unit economics we should price the step-ups at an intermediate rate (not the lowest scale price until they reach 100 GPUs) and include a 12-month minimum commitment for the ladder. If they insist on <12mo, we expose slightly higher unit rates.

Questions for you all: can SRE sign the SLA exception for pre-warm cache retention in multi-tenant nodes? Also, legal needs a short clause for step-up acceptance windows (7 business days) to avoid surprise capacity locks.

If we agree internally I’ll present the scaled Booking Ladder to Jordan + procurement on Friday and push the DocuSign with the adjusted schedule + a clear few-line summary for procurement (monthly invoices, PO flow).

—Ethan

Subject: Re: Capacity booking ladder & GPU cushion options for Sable AI — updated recommendation

Jordan / Priya — thanks for the clarity. Based on your procurement and sizing constraints, here is an updated, actionable offer that should meet finance and security needs while preserving launch reliability.

Finalized offer (Booking Ladder — scaled):
- Initial baseline: 40 committed GPUs (monthly invoice).
- Step-up 1 (wk6): +20 GPUs (monthly billing begins on the step-up effective date).
- Step-up 2 (month3): +40 GPUs, reaching 100 GPUs total if exercised.
- Billing cadence: monthly invoices tied to a single PO number (we’ll amortize onboarding credits across first 3 invoices).
- Commercial term: 12-month minimum. If Sable requires a shorter term we can offer 6 months at +15% unit rate.
- Operational guards: 1 month of pre-warm credits, 10% GPU cushion for surge protection, and a documented fallback flow that redirects low-priority jobs to spot-backed lanes to protect latency for priority endpoints.
- Private deployment: we can queue Sable for Q3 private deployment; this does not block the hosted Dedicated lane activation but will add ~6 weeks to any hardware lead time (we’ll flag this on the MAP).

Attachments: updated capacity-options-worksheet.xlsx (row: "Scaled Booking Ladder — Sable AI"). I’ve also added a short one-page latency & fallback appendix to the MAP. If this looks good I’ll prepare the DocuSign commitment and a succinct procurement summary for your finance lead (single PO, monthly billing).

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick call with procurement (30m) to confirm PO workflow — I’m available Friday 14:00–16:00 PT or Monday morning.
2) Sign DocuSign (I’ll push within 24 hours after your confirmation).
3) Kickoff runbook with our ops team once DocuSign is complete (target activation: 2027-01-15).

If you want any tweaks to the step-up timing or baseline we can model the invoice impact and share a redline in the worksheet.

Best regards,
Ethan Park
